stem: An analyst must establish that one account failed authentication on the VPN, then succeeded, then immediately accessed a file server and triggered an endpoint alert. The three sources store logs separately in different formats. Which capability makes this reconstruction practical?

options.text: Log aggregation into a SIEM, normalized into one timeline
options.why: Aggregation and normalization are what make a cross-source timeline possible at all: one searchable, time-aligned store. Without them the analyst is manually reconciling three formats and three clocks.

options.text: Alert tuning on the endpoint platform to sharpen its detections
options.why: Tuning reduces noise from one source. It does not bring three sources together.

options.text: Archiving the logs from all three sources to long-term storage
options.why: Archiving preserves data for retention. It does not normalize or correlate it.

options.text: Running a vulnerability scan across the three systems involved
options.why: A scan reports weaknesses that exist, not a sequence of events that happened.

stem: An organisation retains security logs for 30 days. Industry figures put its likely time to detect an intrusion at several months. What is the consequence?

options.text: Evidence of how an intrusion began is gone before it is detected
options.why: Retention has to exceed realistic detection time or the investigation starts after the record ends. This is why archiving is a named activity rather than housekeeping. Keep logs longer than it takes to notice.

options.text: None, provided the SIEM correlates events in real time
options.why: Real-time correlation catches what the rules recognise. Everything they missed is what you need the history for.

options.text: Detection will be faster because there is less log data to search
options.why: Search performance is an engineering problem. Deleting evidence does not improve detection.

options.text: Alert tuning will compensate for the shorter retention period
options.why: Tuning changes which alerts fire now. It cannot recover data already deleted.

stem: A network team needs to be notified immediately when a switch interface goes down or a device reboots unexpectedly. Which mechanism is designed for this?

options.text: SNMP traps sent by the device
options.why: A trap is the device pushing an unsolicited notification the moment a condition occurs, which is the difference from polling, where the manager asks on a schedule.

options.text: NetFlow records from the switch
options.why: NetFlow describes traffic conversations: who talked to whom, how much, for how long. It says nothing about device health.

options.text: A scheduled vulnerability scanner
options.why: Enumerates weaknesses on a schedule. It is not an event notification mechanism.

options.text: SCAP content for the devices
options.why: SCAP standardizes how configuration and vulnerability state is expressed for automated checking. It is not an event notification mechanism.

stem: Monitoring can be aimed at systems, applications or infrastructure. Which concern belongs specifically to application monitoring?

options.text: Transaction errors and unusual requests within the application
options.why: Application monitoring sees what the application does and what its users do inside it, such as transaction errors and authentication failures, which no layer beneath it can observe. Inside the app's own logic: application monitoring.

options.text: CPU, memory and disk utilization on the host running the application
options.why: That is system monitoring: the operating system and its resources.

options.text: Switch interface errors and link saturation across the data center
options.why: Infrastructure monitoring, covering the network and facility layer.

options.text: Whether endpoint agents are installed and reporting on each server
options.why: Agent health sits with system and endpoint monitoring.

stem: A security team must assess laptops that are frequently off the corporate network and rarely connected during scheduled scan windows. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Agent-based scanning that reports when online
options.why: The agent travels with the device, assesses locally and reports when connectivity allows, so it does not depend on the asset being reachable at a particular moment, which is the whole trade-off against agentless.

options.text: Agentless network scanning on a tighter schedule
options.why: More frequent scans still only see devices that happen to be connected. The laptops remain invisible.

options.text: SNMP polling of each laptop while it is on site
options.why: SNMP is for network and infrastructure device state and is not how endpoints are assessed for vulnerabilities.

options.text: Reviewing NetFlow records for the laptops' traffic
options.why: Flow data shows conversations, not patch or configuration state.

stem: A DLP rule matches an outbound message containing customer records. The organisation wants the message held for review rather than blocked outright or delivered. Which response is this?

options.text: Quarantine
options.why: Quarantine holds the item pending a decision, which is the middle path between blocking, which breaks legitimate work, and alerting only, which lets the data leave.

options.text: Alert tuning
options.why: Tuning adjusts which conditions raise an alert. It is not a response action applied to a matched item.

options.text: Archiving
options.why: Archiving moves records to long-term storage. It is not an interception action.

options.text: Remediation validation
options.why: That confirms a fix actually worked, after the fact.

stem: A monthly report shows alert volumes, mean time to triage and the proportion of alerts closed as false positives. What is this reporting principally for?

options.text: Measuring whether the monitoring itself is healthy
options.why: Reporting at this level measures the function rather than any one incident, and shows where tuning is needed. A rising false positive rate is the signal that tuning is overdue. Monthly metrics grade the monitor, not the attacker.

options.text: Detecting active intrusions across the environment
options.why: Detection happens through alerting in near real time. A monthly summary is far too late for that.

options.text: Satisfying evidence requirements for chain of custody
options.why: Chain of custody documents handling of specific evidence in an investigation.

options.text: Replacing the need for ongoing alert tuning work
options.why: It indicates that tuning is needed. It does not perform it.

stem: An organisation wants its scanners, configuration tools and reporting to express system state in a common machine-readable format so results can be compared across vendors. Which standard addresses this?

options.text: SCAP
options.why: The Security Content Automation Protocol standardises how vulnerabilities, configuration state and benchmarks are expressed, so different tools produce comparable output.

options.text: NetFlow
options.why: A format for traffic flow records, not for configuration or vulnerability state.

options.text: SNMP
options.why: A protocol for monitoring and managing network devices, not a content standard for security findings.

options.text: SIEM
options.why: A category of product that collects and correlates events, not a standard for expressing state.

stem: Which TWO statements about a security monitoring pipeline are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Correlation turns events from many sources into a single actionable alert
options.why: Aggregation puts data in one place; correlation is the stage that produces meaning from it. Aggregation collects, correlation connects.

options.text: Retention must outlast realistic detection time, or evidence is gone first
options.why: Archiving decisions directly bound what any future investigation can establish. Keep logs longer than it takes to notice.

options.text: A high false positive rate is harmless because analysts can ignore those alerts
options.why: It is the main cause of real alerts being missed, which is why tuning is a named activity.

options.text: Aggregation and correlation are simply two names for the same pipeline stage
options.why: One collects and normalizes; the other applies rules across what was collected.

options.text: Monthly reporting is the primary mechanism for detecting intrusions
options.why: Reporting measures the function over time. Detection is near real time.

stem: You need to find which internal hosts communicated with a known command and control address over the past six weeks. Which data source is designed for this?

options.text: NetFlow records
options.why: Flow data records who talked to whom, how much and for how long, and it is small enough to retain for weeks.

options.text: Full packet capture
options.why: Packet capture carries contents and is far too large to hold for six weeks at any scale. You rarely need the payload to answer 'who talked to this address'.

options.text: SCAP benchmark results
options.why: SCAP reports whether a host matches a configuration standard. It sees no traffic.

options.text: SNMP traps from the core switches
options.why: Traps report a device's own state changes, not conversations between hosts.

stem: An auditor asks for evidence that 400 servers match the agreed hardening benchmark. Which tool produces it?

options.text: A SCAP benchmark compliance scan
options.why: SCAP exists to express a benchmark in machine-readable form and report compliance against it, host by host.

options.text: A SIEM correlation search
options.why: A SIEM correlates events that happened. It does not evaluate a host's current configuration against a standard.

options.text: NetFlow analysis
options.why: Flow data describes traffic, not configuration.

options.text: A packet capture on the server VLAN
options.why: Traffic contents say nothing about whether a host is hardened.

stem: Analysts receive 600 alerts a day, almost all benign, and have started closing them in bulk without reading. What is the correct response?

options.text: Alert tuning to suppress known-good patterns
options.why: This is alert fatigue, and the cure is fewer, better alerts: raise thresholds and suppress known-good patterns. An alert nobody reads provides no detection at all.

options.text: Add more detection rules to improve coverage
options.why: More alerts into a queue nobody reads makes the real one less likely to be seen, not more.

options.text: Quarantine the endpoints that raise the alerts
options.why: Quarantine is a containment action against one confirmed threat. There is no confirmed threat here, there is noise.

options.text: Discipline the analysts for closing alerts unread
options.why: The behaviour is a rational response to an unworkable queue. The finding is the queue.

stem: An endpoint tool confirms a malicious executable on a laptop. Which alert response action is this?

options.text: Quarantine
options.why: Isolating the confirmed malicious object or host is the named alert response action, and it buys time to investigate.

options.text: Alert tuning
options.why: Tuning adjusts which alerts fire. This alert was correct and needs acting on.

options.text: Log aggregation
options.why: Aggregation brings logs together so they can be correlated. It is not a response to a confirmed detection.

options.text: Archiving
options.why: Archiving retains data for later. It does nothing about the live file.

stem: A fleet includes appliances where no software may be installed. Which monitoring approach fits, and what is the trade?

options.text: Agentless, trading depth of visibility for no install
options.why: Agentless collection works where you cannot deploy software, at the cost of depth and of needing network access and credentials or protocols that reach the device. No install allowed: agentless, with less depth.

options.text: Agent based, because it gives richer data from each device
options.why: Richer, and the scenario says no software may be installed, which rules it out.

options.text: Neither, because appliances cannot be monitored at all
options.why: Agentless collection exists precisely for this case.

options.text: Install agents anyway and accept the vendor support risk
options.why: On a vendor appliance this usually voids support and may be technically impossible.

stem: An auditor asks for evidence of authentication failures from eleven months ago, though the SIEM only holds 90 days of searchable data. Which stage of the pipeline should have kept it?

options.text: Archiving
options.why: Archiving keeps older logs in cheaper storage for compliance and later investigation.

options.text: Alerting
options.why: Alerting notifies on events as they happen. It does not preserve them.

options.text: Reporting
options.why: Reports summarise data that already exists. They do not store raw logs.

options.text: Quarantine
options.why: Quarantine isolates a suspect item. It has nothing to do with log retention.

stem: A rule fires 400 times a day and almost every alert is benign, so analysts have started ignoring it. What is the best fix?

options.text: Tune the rule to cut false positives
options.why: Tuning restores signal and keeps analysts trusting alerts, while the rule still catches the real events. Noisy rule, real events: tune it, do not disable it.

options.text: Disable the rule until the noise stops
options.why: Disabling removes detection entirely, trading noise for blindness.

options.text: Raise every alert to the highest priority
options.why: Making all alerts urgent makes the noise worse.

options.text: Quarantine the hosts that trigger it
options.why: Quarantine is a response to confirmed malicious items. Benign alerts need tuning.

stem: An organisation wants a record of which hosts talked to which, how often, and how much data moved, without storing full packet payloads. Which tool fits?

options.text: NetFlow
options.why: NetFlow summarises conversations with addresses, ports, timing and volume, without payloads.

options.text: SNMP traps
options.why: Traps notify of device events such as an interface going down. They do not describe traffic.

options.text: SCAP
options.why: SCAP is a standard for expressing and checking configuration and vulnerability state.

options.text: An antivirus scan
options.why: Antivirus examines files for malware. It does not report network conversations.

stem: After patching a critical flaw on 200 servers, the team wants proof the vulnerability is gone. Which action provides it?

options.text: Rescan the servers to confirm the finding is gone
options.why: A rescan after remediation validates that the fix worked on all 200 servers. Patched is a claim; a clean rescan is the evidence.

options.text: Close the ticket because the patch job reported success
options.why: A deployment report shows the patch ran, not that the flaw is gone.

options.text: Review next month's vulnerability dashboard
options.why: A dashboard may not show the specific finding, and the wait leaves exposure.

options.text: Archive the original scan report as evidence
options.why: Archiving keeps evidence of the old state and proves nothing about the fix.
